source.text: מַשָּׂ֤א דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַדְרָ֔ךְ וְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק מְנֻחָת֑וֹ כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ עֵ֣ין אָדָ֔ם וְכֹ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Oracle. [The] word of Yahweh [is] against [the] land of Hadrach, and Damascus [is] its resting place; for to Yahweh [is the] eye of humankind and all [the] tribes of Israel,

en.L: An oracle. The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] against the land of Hadrach, \q and Damascus [is] its resting place; \q for to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [belongs the] eye on humankind \q and on all the tribes of Israel,
en.B: An oracle. The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is against the land of Hadrach, \q and Damascus is where it will come to rest; \q for the eye of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is on all humankind \q and on all the tribes of Israel,
en.R: This is a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is against the land of Hadrach, \q and it will come down on the city of Damascus. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} watches over all people, \q and over all the tribes of Israel too.

es.L: Oráculo. La palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [está] contra la tierra de Hadrac, \q y Damasco [es] su lugar de reposo; \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [tiene] el ojo puesto en la humanidad \q y en todas las tribus de Israel,
es.B: Oráculo. La palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está contra la tierra de Hadrac, \q y en Damasco vendrá a posarse; \q porque el ojo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está sobre toda la humanidad \q y sobre todas las tribus de Israel,
es.R: Este es un mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Es contra la tierra de Hadrac, \q y caerá sobre la ciudad de Damasco. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vigila a todas las personas, \q y también a todas las tribus de Israel.

fr.L: Oracle. La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [est] contre le pays de Hadrak, \q et Damas [est] son lieu de repos ; \q car {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} [appartient] l’œil sur l’humanité \q et sur toutes les tribus d’Israël,
fr.B: Oracle. La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est contre le pays de Hadrak, \q et c’est sur Damas qu’elle se posera ; \q car l’œil {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est sur toute l’humanité \q et sur toutes les tribus d’Israël,
fr.R: Voici un message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Il est contre le pays de Hadrak, \q et il s’abattra sur la ville de Damas. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} veille sur tous les humains, \q et aussi sur toutes les tribus d’Israël.

sw.L: Unabii. Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [li] juu ya nchi ya Hadraki, \q na Dameski [ni] mahali pake pa kupumzika; \q kwa maana jicho la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [li] juu ya wanadamu \q na juu ya makabila yote ya Israeli,
sw.B: Unabii. Neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni dhidi ya nchi ya Hadraki, \q na litatua juu ya Dameski; \q kwa maana jicho la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} liko juu ya wanadamu wote \q na juu ya makabila yote ya Israeli,
sw.R: Huu ni ujumbe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ni dhidi ya nchi ya Hadraki, \q nao utaushukia mji wa Dameski. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anawaangalia watu wote, \q na makabila yote ya Israeli pia.

vi.L: Sấm ngôn. Lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [nghịch cùng] xứ Ha-đơ-rắc, \q và Đa-mách [là] nơi nó dừng lại; \q vì mắt của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [đoái xem] loài người \q và mọi chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên,
vi.B: Sấm ngôn. Lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nghịch cùng xứ Ha-đơ-rắc, \q và sẽ dừng lại trên Đa-mách; \q vì mắt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đoái xem cả loài người \q và mọi chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên,
vi.R: Đây là sứ điệp của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Sứ điệp này nghịch cùng xứ Ha-đơ-rắc, \q và sẽ giáng xuống thành Đa-mách. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trông chừng mọi người, \q và cả mọi chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên nữa.

ko.L: 신탁. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 하드락 땅을 [치고], \q 다메섹이 그 [말씀이] 머물 곳이다. \q 사람들 위에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈이 있고 \q 이스라엘의 모든 지파 위에도 [있기] 때문이다.
ko.B: 신탁. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 하드락 땅을 치고, \q 다메섹에 내려 머물 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 온 인류를 눈여겨보시고 \q 이스라엘의 모든 지파도 눈여겨보시기 때문이다.
ko.R: 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이다. 이 말씀은 하드락 땅을 치고, \q 다메섹 성에 내릴 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 모든 사람을 지켜보신다. \q 이스라엘의 모든 지파도 지켜보신다.

decisions.choice: oracle: the heading of a new part of the book (chapters 9-11), as again at 12:1
decisions.reason: Chapters 1-8 are dated to the reign of Darius and tell of Zechariah's visions and sermons. Chapters 9-14 have no dates and no visions. They fall into two parts, each headed with the same words, "An oracle. The word of the LORD" (9:1; 12:1); Malachi 1:1 opens with the same heading. The word for "oracle" comes from the verb "lift up". It is a solemn pronouncement from God, often a word of judgment on a nation, as in the oracles on the nations in Isaiah 13-23. Most of chapters 9-10 are poetry.

decisions.choice: Hadrach and Damascus: the land of Aram (Syria), north of Israel
decisions.reason: Hadrach is named only here in the Bible. It is usually identified with a city and region in northern Syria, near Hamath, that Assyrian records call Hatarikka. Damascus was the chief city of Aram. The oracle begins in the far north and moves south through Hamath (verse 2), along the coast through Tyre and Sidon (verses 2-4), to the cities of the Philistines (verses 5-7): the lands on Israel's borders that had long been its enemies.

decisions.choice: Damascus is its resting place: the word of the LORD will settle on Damascus
decisions.reason: The word of judgment is pictured as something that goes out and comes to rest on a place, as a load is set down. The same noun is used of the LORD's resting place in Zion (Psalm 132:14). The point is that the word will not pass Damascus by.

decisions.choice: to the LORD belongs the eye on humankind: the LORD watches over all people, Israel included
alternatives: the eyes of all people and of all the tribes of Israel are on the LORD
the eye of Aram belongs to the LORD (a change of one letter)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "for to the LORD [is the] eye of humankind and all the tribes of Israel". It is read here as saying that the LORD keeps watch over all the nations as well as over Israel, so that what happens to the cities named is his doing. It can also be read the other way round: the eyes of all people, and of all Israel's tribes, are turned toward the LORD as they see what he does. A small change to one letter of the word for "humankind" gives "Aram" (Syria), and some read "for the eye (or "the chief city") of Aram belongs to the LORD, as do all the tribes of Israel". The written Hebrew is translated here.

decisions.choice: An oracle (L, B); a message from the LORD (R); comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: Massa' is "oracle" at Literal and Balanced and "message" at Readable, as in Isaiah. Balanced says "where it will come to rest" for "its resting place". Readable names Damascus as a city and says plainly what the eye of the LORD means (m4). The sentence runs on into verse 2, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

decisions.choice: "Oráculo" (L, B); "Este es un mensaje" (R); "Hadrac"
decisions.reason: Massa is "Oráculo" at Literal and Balanced and "mensaje" at Readable, as Isaiah and 12:1. Hadrach is a new name, spelled as Spanish writes Hebrew names.

decisions.choice: "Oracle" (L, B); "Voici un message" (R); "Hadrak"
decisions.reason: Massa as Isaiah and 12:1; "Hadrak" as the names table.

decisions.choice: "Unabii" (L, B); "ujumbe" (R); "Hadraki"
decisions.reason: Massa as Isaiah and 12:1; Hadrach is new, with a final vowel after the closed syllable.

decisions.choice: "Sấm ngôn" (L, B); "sứ điệp" (R); "Ha-đơ-rắc"
decisions.reason: Massa as Isaiah and 12:1; the name as the names table.

decisions.choice: "신탁" (L, B), "…의 말씀이다" (R); each verse closes as its own sentence
decisions.reason: Massa as 12:1. The Hebrew sentence runs on into verse 2; Korean ends each verse with its own verb, as the Psalms do, and verse 2 goes on with the places the word comes on. The prophet speaks about God here, so "눈여겨보시고" takes -시-.

source.text: וְגַם־חֲמָ֖ת תִּגְבָּל־בָּ֑הּ צֹ֣ר וְצִיד֔וֹן כִּ֥י חָֽכְמָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: and also Hamath [which] borders on it, Tyre and Sidon, for it is very wise.

en.L: and also Hamath, which borders on it, \q Tyre and Sidon, for she [is] very wise.
en.B: and on Hamath too, which borders it, \q and on Tyre and Sidon, wise as they think they are.
en.R: It is also against the city of Hamath, near Damascus, \q and against Tyre and Sidon, even though they think they are very wise.

es.L: y también Hamat, que limita con ella, \q Tiro y Sidón, porque es muy sabia.
es.B: y también contra Hamat, que linda con ella, \q y contra Tiro y Sidón, por más sabias que se crean.
es.R: También es contra la ciudad de Hamat, cerca de Damasco, \q y contra Tiro y Sidón, aunque se creen muy sabias.

fr.L: et aussi Hamath, qui la borde, \q Tyr et Sidon, car elle [est] très sage.
fr.B: et contre Hamath aussi, sa voisine, \q et contre Tyr et Sidon, si sages qu’elles se croient.
fr.R: Il est aussi contre la ville de Hamath, près de Damas, \q et contre Tyr et Sidon, même si elles se croient très sages.

sw.L: na pia Hamathi, inayopakana nayo, \q Tiro na Sidoni, kwa maana ni wenye hekima sana.
sw.B: na juu ya Hamathi pia, inayopakana nayo, \q na juu ya Tiro na Sidoni, ingawa wanajiona kuwa wenye hekima.
sw.R: Ni dhidi ya mji wa Hamathi pia, karibu na Dameski, \q na dhidi ya Tiro na Sidoni, ingawa wanadhani kwamba wana hekima nyingi.

vi.L: và cả Ha-mát, là nơi giáp ranh với nó, \q Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, vì nó rất khôn ngoan.
vi.B: và nghịch cùng Ha-mát nữa, là nơi giáp ranh với nó, \q cùng Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, dù chúng tự cho mình rất khôn ngoan.
vi.R: Sứ điệp ấy cũng nghịch cùng thành Ha-mát, gần Đa-mách, \q và nghịch cùng Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, dù chúng nghĩ mình rất khôn ngoan.

ko.L: 또한 그 땅과 경계를 맞댄 하맛과, \q 두로와 시돈에도 [임한다]. 그 성이 매우 지혜롭기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 땅과 맞닿은 하맛에도 임하고, \q 스스로 지혜롭다고 여기는 두로와 시돈에도 임할 것이다.
ko.R: 이 말씀은 다메섹 가까이에 있는 하맛 성도 치고, \q 스스로 매우 지혜롭다고 생각하는 두로와 시돈도 칠 것이다.

decisions.choice: Hamath, Tyre and Sidon: a Syrian city to the north, and the two great Phoenician ports on the coast
decisions.reason: Hamath stood on the Orontes river, north of Damascus. Tyre and Sidon were the chief cities of Phoenicia, on the coast north of Israel, rich from trade by sea. The word of judgment moves from Syria to the coast.

decisions.choice: for she is very wise: said with irony of Tyre's cleverness in trade
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine singular, so it speaks of Tyre in the first place, with Sidon beside it. Ezekiel 28:3-5 mocks the king of Tyre as "wiser than Daniel", a wisdom that had made him rich and proud. The next verse shows what that wisdom had built; verse 4 shows that it will not save the city. The word "for" may also be read "though": though she is very wise.

decisions.choice: and on ... too (B); It is also against (R); wise as they think they are (B); even though they think they are very wise (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable carry on the sense of verse 1, that the word is against these places. They bring out the irony of "very wise" (m2) by saying that the cities think themselves wise, and they speak of Tyre and Sidon together.

decisions.choice: "car elle [est] très sage", Tyre in the feminine
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is feminine singular and speaks of Tyre as a woman; Balanced and Readable speak of both cities, as the English.

source.text: וַתִּ֥בֶן צֹ֛ר מָצ֖וֹר לָ֑הּ וַתִּצְבָּר־כֶּ֨סֶף֙ כֶּֽעָפָ֔ר וְחָר֖וּץ כְּטִ֥יט חוּצֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And built Tyre a fortress for herself, and heaped up silver like dust, and gold like [the] mud of [the] streets.

en.L: And Tyre built herself a fortress, \q and heaped up silver like dust \q and fine gold like the mud of [the] streets.
en.B: Tyre has built herself a fortress; \q she has piled up silver like dust, \q and gold like mud in the streets.
en.R: The city of Tyre built strong walls to protect itself. \q It piled up silver as if it were dust, \q and gold as if it were mud in the streets.

es.L: Y Tiro se edificó una fortaleza, \q y amontonó plata como polvo \q y oro fino como el lodo de [las] calles.
es.B: Tiro se ha construido una fortaleza; \q ha amontonado plata como polvo, \q y oro como lodo en las calles.
es.R: La ciudad de Tiro construyó fuertes murallas para protegerse. \q Amontonó plata como si fuera polvo, \q y oro como si fuera lodo en las calles.

fr.L: Et Tyr s’est bâti une forteresse, \q et elle a amassé l’argent comme la poussière \q et l’or fin comme la boue des rues.
fr.B: Tyr s’est bâti une forteresse ; \q elle a entassé l’argent comme de la poussière, \q et l’or comme la boue des rues.
fr.R: La ville de Tyr a construit de solides murailles pour se protéger. \q Elle a entassé l’argent comme si c’était de la poussière, \q et l’or comme si c’était de la boue dans les rues.

sw.L: Na Tiro ilijijengea ngome, \q ikalundika fedha kama mavumbi, \q na dhahabu safi kama tope la njiani.
sw.B: Tiro imejijengea ngome; \q imelundika fedha kama mavumbi, \q na dhahabu kama tope la barabarani.
sw.R: Mji wa Tiro ulijenga kuta imara ili ujilinde. \q Ulilundika fedha kana kwamba ni mavumbi, \q na dhahabu kana kwamba ni tope barabarani.

vi.L: Ty-rơ đã xây cho mình một đồn lũy, \q chất bạc như bụi đất, \q và vàng ròng như bùn [ngoài] đường phố.
vi.B: Ty-rơ đã xây cho mình một đồn lũy; \q nó chất bạc như bụi, \q và vàng như bùn ngoài đường.
vi.R: Thành Ty-rơ xây tường thành kiên cố để tự bảo vệ. \q Nó chất bạc như thể bạc là bụi đất, \q và chất vàng như thể vàng là bùn ngoài đường.

ko.L: 두로가 자기를 위하여 요새를 짓고, \q 은을 티끌같이 쌓고 \q 순금을 거리의 진흙같이 [쌓았다].
ko.B: 두로는 스스로 요새를 쌓았다. \q 은을 티끌처럼 쌓아 올리고, \q 금을 거리의 진흙처럼 쌓았다.
ko.R: 두로 성은 자기를 지키려고 튼튼한 성벽을 쌓았다. \q 은을 마치 먼지처럼 쌓아 두었고, \q 금을 마치 길거리의 진흙처럼 쌓아 두었다.

decisions.choice: Tyre built a fortress: a play on the city's name
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name Tyre (Tsor) means "rock", and the word for "fortress" (matsor) sounds almost the same. Tyre stood on a rocky island just off the coast, protected by the sea and by high walls, and it held out against long sieges by Assyria and by Nebuchadnezzar (Ezekiel 26-29). It was famous for being hard to take.

decisions.choice: silver like dust, gold like the mud of the streets: wealth beyond counting
decisions.reason: Dust and street mud are what is most common and least valued. Tyre's trade had made silver and gold as common as dirt; 1 Kings 10:27 says the same of silver in Solomon's Jerusalem. Ezekiel 27 lists the riches that came to Tyre by sea. The word used for gold is a poetic word for fine gold.

decisions.choice: The city of Tyre; strong walls to protect itself (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that Tyre is a city and that its fortress was its walls, and uses "it" for the city where the Hebrew speaks of it as "she".

source.text: הִנֵּ֤ה אֲדֹנָי֙ יֽוֹרִשֶׁ֔נָּה וְהִכָּ֥ה בַיָּ֖ם חֵילָ֑הּ וְהִ֖יא בָּאֵ֥שׁ תֵּאָכֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, [the] Lord will dispossess her, and he will strike into the sea her strength, and she by fire will be consumed.

en.L: Look, the Lord will dispossess her \q and strike her strength into the sea, \q and she will be consumed by fire.
en.B: But look, the Lord will strip her of all she has \q and hurl her power down into the sea, \q and she will be burned up with fire.
en.R: But the Lord will take away everything she owns. \q He will throw her power into the sea, \q and the city will be burned to the ground.

es.L: He aquí, el Señor la despojará \q y arrojará al mar su fuerza, \q y ella será consumida por el fuego.
es.B: Pero mira, el Señor la despojará de todo lo que tiene \q y lanzará su poder al fondo del mar, \q y será consumida por el fuego.
es.R: Pero el Señor le quitará todo lo que tiene. \q Arrojará al mar su poder, \q y la ciudad será quemada hasta los cimientos.

fr.L: Voici, le Seigneur la dépossédera \q et frappera sa force dans la mer, \q et elle sera dévorée par le feu.
fr.B: Mais voici que le Seigneur la dépouillera de tout ce qu’elle a \q et précipitera sa puissance dans la mer, \q et elle sera consumée par le feu.
fr.R: Mais le Seigneur lui prendra tout ce qu’elle possède. \q Il jettera sa puissance dans la mer, \q et la ville sera entièrement brûlée.

sw.L: Tazama, Bwana atainyang'anya mali yake \q na kuipiga nguvu yake baharini, \q nayo itateketezwa kwa moto.
sw.B: Lakini tazama, Bwana ataivua kila kitu ilicho nacho, \q na kuitupa nguvu yake chini baharini, \q nayo itateketezwa kwa moto.
sw.R: Lakini Bwana atainyang'anya kila kitu ilicho nacho. \q Atatupa nguvu zake baharini, \q na mji huo utateketezwa kabisa kwa moto.

vi.L: Kìa, Chúa sẽ tước đoạt nó, \q đánh sức mạnh nó xuống biển, \q và nó sẽ bị lửa thiêu nuốt.
vi.B: Nhưng kìa, Chúa sẽ tước đoạt mọi thứ nó có, \q ném sức mạnh nó xuống biển, \q và nó sẽ bị lửa thiêu rụi.
vi.R: Nhưng Chúa sẽ lấy đi mọi thứ nó có. \q Ngài sẽ ném sức mạnh của nó xuống biển, \q và thành ấy sẽ bị thiêu rụi.

ko.L: 보라, 주님께서 그 성을 빼앗으시고 \q 그 힘을 바다에 쳐 넣으시니, \q 그 성은 불에 삼켜질 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 보아라, 주님께서 그 성이 가진 모든 것을 빼앗으시고 \q 그 힘을 바닷속에 던져 버리실 것이다. \q 그 성은 불에 타 버릴 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 주님께서 그 성이 가진 것을 모두 빼앗으실 것이다. \q 그 힘을 바다에 던져 버리실 것이다. \q 그 성은 불에 타서 잿더미가 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: dispossess her: take away all she possesses
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for taking possession of a land and driving out those who held it. Here the Lord takes from Tyre the wealth of verse 3. The city that trusted in its walls and its riches will lose both.

decisions.choice: strike her strength into the sea: destroy her power, which was on the sea
alternatives: strike her rampart into the sea
strike her wealth into the sea
decisions.reason: The noun can mean strength, wealth or an army; a similar word means a rampart. Tyre's power, its wealth and its walls all stood on the sea, and the Lord will throw it down into the sea. Ezekiel 26:12 and 27:27 picture Tyre's wealth sinking into the sea. Read as "rampart", the line pictures the city's sea wall struck down into the water; the sense is close.

decisions.choice: she will be consumed by fire: the burning of a captured city
decisions.reason: A conquered city was burned (Amos 1:10 says the same of Tyre). Tyre was finally taken by storm and burned by Alexander the Great in 332 BC, after he built a causeway out to the island; many readers see that event here. The oracle does not name the conqueror: it is the Lord who acts.

decisions.choice: But look (B); But (R); strip her of all she has (B); take away everything she owns (R); hurl her power down (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "but" to mark the turn from Tyre's pride in verse 3 to its fall. They spell out "dispossess" (m1), and say "power" for "strength" (m2). Readable says "the city" for "she".

decisions.choice: "주님" for Adonai, with -시-; "그 성" for Tyre
decisions.reason: Adonai alone is 주님, kept apart from the divine name; the prophet speaks about God, so the honorific is used. Tyre is "그 성", never "그녀".

source.text: תֵּרֶ֨א אַשְׁקְל֜וֹן וְתִירָ֗א וְעַזָּה֙ וְתָחִ֣יל מְאֹ֔ד וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּֽי־הֹבִ֣ישׁ מֶבָּטָ֑הּ וְאָ֤בַד מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ מֵֽעַזָּ֔ה וְאַשְׁקְל֖וֹן לֹ֥א תֵשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: Will see Ashkelon and be afraid, and Gaza, and will writhe greatly, and Ekron, for is put to shame her hope; and will perish a king from Gaza, and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.

en.L: Ashkelon will see [it] and be afraid, and Gaza [will] writhe greatly, \q and Ekron, for her hope has been put to shame; \q and a king will perish from Gaza, \q and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.
en.B: Ashkelon will see it and be afraid; Gaza will twist in pain, \q and Ekron too, for what she trusted in has failed. \q Gaza will lose her king, \q and Ashkelon will be left empty.
en.R: The people of Ashkelon will see it and be terrified. Gaza will shake with fear, \q and so will Ekron, because what it trusted in has failed. \q Gaza will have no king any longer, \q and no one will live in Ashkelon.

es.L: Lo verá Ascalón y temerá, y Gaza se retorcerá mucho, \q y Ecrón, porque su esperanza ha sido avergonzada; \q y perecerá el rey de Gaza, \q y Ascalón no será habitada.
es.B: Ascalón lo verá y tendrá miedo; Gaza se retorcerá de dolor, \q y también Ecrón, porque aquello en que confiaba le ha fallado. \q Gaza se quedará sin rey, \q y Ascalón quedará deshabitada.
es.R: La gente de Ascalón lo verá y se llenará de terror. Gaza temblará de miedo, \q y también Ecrón, porque aquello en que confiaba le ha fallado. \q Gaza ya no tendrá rey, \q y nadie vivirá en Ascalón.

fr.L: Ashqelôn le verra et aura peur, et Gaza se tordra de douleur, \q et Eqrôn, car son espérance est confondue ; \q et le roi disparaîtra de Gaza, \q et Ashqelôn ne sera plus habitée.
fr.B: Ashqelôn le verra et aura peur ; Gaza se tordra de douleur, \q et Eqrôn aussi, car ce en quoi elle espérait l’a déçue. \q Gaza perdra son roi, \q et Ashqelôn sera vidée de ses habitants.
fr.R: Les habitants d’Ashqelôn le verront et seront terrifiés. Gaza tremblera de peur, \q et Eqrôn aussi, car ce en quoi elle avait confiance l’a déçue. \q Gaza n’aura plus de roi, \q et personne n’habitera plus Ashqelôn.

sw.L: Ashkeloni itaona na kuogopa, na Gaza itagaagaa kwa uchungu sana, \q na Ekroni, kwa maana tumaini lake limeaibishwa; \q na mfalme ataangamia kutoka Gaza, \q na Ashkeloni haitakaliwa na watu.
sw.B: Ashkeloni itaona na kuogopa; Gaza itagaagaa kwa maumivu, \q na Ekroni pia, kwa maana kile ilichokitumainia kimeshindwa. \q Gaza itampoteza mfalme wake, \q na Ashkeloni itaachwa tupu.
sw.R: Watu wa Ashkeloni wataona hayo na kuogopa sana. Gaza itatetemeka kwa hofu, \q na Ekroni pia, kwa sababu kile ilichokitegemea kimeshindwa. \q Gaza haitakuwa na mfalme tena, \q na hakuna mtu atakayeishi Ashkeloni.

vi.L: Ách-kê-lôn sẽ thấy và sợ hãi, và Ga-xa sẽ quặn thắt rất nhiều, \q và Éc-rôn nữa, vì niềm trông cậy của nó bị hổ thẹn; \q vua sẽ bị diệt khỏi Ga-xa, \q và Ách-kê-lôn sẽ không còn người ở.
vi.B: Ách-kê-lôn sẽ thấy và sợ hãi; Ga-xa sẽ quặn đau, \q Éc-rôn cũng vậy, vì điều nó tin cậy đã thất bại. \q Ga-xa sẽ mất vua, \q và Ách-kê-lôn sẽ bị bỏ hoang.
vi.R: Dân Ách-kê-lôn sẽ thấy và kinh hãi. Ga-xa sẽ run sợ, \q Éc-rôn cũng vậy, vì điều nó tin cậy đã thất bại. \q Ga-xa sẽ không còn vua nữa, \q và không ai sống ở Ách-kê-lôn.

ko.L: 아스글론이 보고 두려워하며, 가사도 몹시 몸부림칠 것이다. \q 에그론도 그러할 것이니, 그 소망이 부끄러움을 당했기 때문이다. \q 가사에서 왕이 끊어지고, \q 아스글론에는 사람이 살지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 아스글론이 그것을 보고 두려워하고, 가사가 고통으로 몸부림칠 것이다. \q 에그론도 그러할 것이니, 믿고 바라던 것이 무너졌기 때문이다. \q 가사는 왕을 잃고, \q 아스글론은 텅 비게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 아스글론 사람들이 그것을 보고 몹시 무서워할 것이다. 가사는 두려워 떨 것이고, \q 에그론도 그러할 것이다. 그들이 믿던 것이 무너졌기 때문이다. \q 가사에는 더 이상 왕이 없을 것이고, \q 아스글론에는 아무도 살지 않을 것이다.

decisions.choice: Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron (and Ashdod in verse 6): four cities of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Philistines lived on the southern coastal plain, in five chief cities: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron and Gath (1 Samuel 6:17). Gath is missing here, as it is in the oracles against the Philistines in Amos 1:6-8, Jeremiah 25:20 and Zephaniah 2:4; it had probably lost its importance long before.

decisions.choice: her hope has been put to shame: what Ekron trusted in has let her down
decisions.reason: The noun means the thing one looks to with hope or confidence. The Philistine cities had looked to the strength of Tyre and the north to hold back the danger. When Tyre falls (verse 4), they see that their hope was empty, and they are put to shame.

decisions.choice: a king will perish from Gaza; Ashkelon will not be inhabited: the cities will lose their rulers and their people
decisions.reason: A city without its king has lost its independence; a city without inhabitants has been destroyed. Amos 1:8 uses the same pair of pictures of Ashdod and Ashkelon.

decisions.choice: twist in pain (B); shake with fear (R); left empty (B); no one will live (R)
decisions.reason: The verb "writhe" is used of a woman in labor and of shaking with fear; Balanced keeps the picture of pain, Readable gives the sense. Readable speaks of the people of the cities, who are the ones afraid.

source.text: וְיָשַׁ֥ב מַמְזֵ֖ר בְּאַשְׁדּ֑וֹד וְהִכְרַתִּ֖י גְּא֥וֹן פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And will dwell a mixed people in Ashdod, and I will cut off [the] pride of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And a mixed people will dwell in Ashdod, \q and I will cut off the Philistines' pride.
en.B: A people of mixed birth will settle in Ashdod, \q and I will cut down the pride of the Philistines.
en.R: People from many nations will settle in Ashdod. \q I will put an end to the pride of the Philistines.

es.L: Y un pueblo mezclado habitará en Asdod, \q y cortaré el orgullo de los filisteos.
es.B: Un pueblo de origen mezclado se asentará en Asdod, \q y abatiré el orgullo de los filisteos.
es.R: Gente de muchas naciones se asentará en Asdod. \q Pondré fin al orgullo de los filisteos.

fr.L: Et un peuple mêlé habitera à Ashdod, \q et je retrancherai l’orgueil des Philistins.
fr.B: Une population de sang mêlé s’installera à Ashdod, \q et j’abattrai l’orgueil des Philistins.
fr.R: Des gens de nombreuses nations s’installeront à Ashdod. \q Je mettrai fin à l’orgueil des Philistins.

sw.L: Na watu wa mchanganyiko watakaa katika Ashdodi, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakatilia mbali kiburi cha Wafilisti.
sw.B: Watu wa damu mchanganyiko watakaa Ashdodi, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakivunja kiburi cha Wafilisti.
sw.R: Watu kutoka mataifa mengi watakaa Ashdodi. \q Nitakomesha kiburi cha Wafilisti.

vi.L: Một dân lai tạp sẽ ở tại Ách-đốt, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ diệt trừ sự kiêu ngạo của người Phi-li-tin.
vi.B: Một dân lai sẽ định cư tại Ách-đốt, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ hạ sự kiêu ngạo của người Phi-li-tin.
vi.R: Người từ nhiều nước sẽ đến ở Ách-đốt. \q Ta sẽ chấm dứt sự kiêu ngạo của người Phi-li-tin.

ko.L: 섞인 백성이 아스돗에 살 것이며, \q 내가 블레셋 사람들의 교만을 끊을 것이다.
ko.B: 혼혈 족속이 아스돗에 자리 잡을 것이며, \q 내가 블레셋 사람들의 교만을 꺾을 것이다.
ko.R: 여러 민족에서 온 사람들이 아스돗에 자리 잡을 것이다. \q 내가 블레셋 사람들의 교만을 끝장낼 것이다.

decisions.choice: a mixed people: people of mixed or doubtful descent
alternatives: a person of illegitimate birth (as Deuteronomy 23:3)
decisions.reason: The word appears elsewhere only in Deuteronomy 23:3, where it describes someone born of a forbidden union, who may not enter the assembly of the LORD. Here it seems to mean a mixed population of foreigners settled in Ashdod in place of its own people, as conquerors often moved peoples from land to land (2 Kings 17:24). The Philistines would no longer be a people of their own.

decisions.choice: I will cut off: the LORD now speaks in his own voice
decisions.reason: Verses 1-5 speak of the LORD in the third person. From here to verse 8 the LORD himself speaks: he is the one who brings down the Philistines' pride, and he will guard his house.

decisions.choice: People from many nations (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "a mixed people" (m1) without the hard edge of the Hebrew word, which it cannot carry plainly.

decisions.choice: God speaks as "Ta" from here on in the poem
decisions.reason: The speaker changes to the LORD himself ("I will cut off"); "Ta" takes the setting in mid-sentence.

source.text: וַהֲסִרֹתִ֨י דָמָ֜יו מִפִּ֗יו וְשִׁקֻּצָיו֙ מִבֵּ֣ין שִׁנָּ֔יו וְנִשְׁאַ֥ר גַּם־ה֖וּא לֵֽאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְהָיָה֙ כְּאַלֻּ֣ף בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּיבוּסִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will remove his blood from his mouth, and his detestable things from between his teeth; and will be left also he for our God, and he will be like a clan in Judah, and Ekron like [the] Jebusite.

en.L: And I will remove its blood from its mouth, and its detestable things from between its teeth; \q and it too will be a remnant for our God, \q and it will be like a clan in Judah, \q and Ekron like the Jebusite.
en.B: I will take the blood out of their mouths and the forbidden food from between their teeth. \q Those who are left will belong to our God; \q they will become one of the clans of Judah, \q and Ekron will be like the Jebusites.
en.R: I will take away the meat with blood still in it from their mouths, and the unclean food from between their teeth. \q Those who are left will belong to our God. \q They will be like a family group in Judah. \q Ekron will become part of God's people, as the Jebusites did.

es.L: Y quitaré su sangre de su boca, y sus cosas detestables de entre sus dientes; \q y también él quedará como remanente para nuestro Dios, \q y será como un clan en Judá, \q y Ecrón como el jebuseo.
es.B: Les quitaré la sangre de la boca y la comida prohibida de entre los dientes. \q Los que queden pertenecerán a nuestro Dios; \q serán como uno de los clanes de Judá, \q y Ecrón será como los jebuseos.
es.R: Les quitaré de la boca la carne que todavía tiene sangre, y de entre los dientes la comida impura. \q Los que queden pertenecerán a nuestro Dios. \q Serán como una familia de Judá. \q Ecrón llegará a formar parte del pueblo de Dios, como les pasó a los jebuseos.

fr.L: Et j’ôterai son sang de sa bouche, et ses choses détestables d’entre ses dents ; \q et lui aussi sera un reste pour notre Dieu, \q et il sera comme un clan en Juda, \q et Eqrôn comme le Jébusien.
fr.B: J’ôterai le sang de leur bouche et les aliments interdits d’entre leurs dents. \q Ceux qui resteront appartiendront à notre Dieu ; \q ils deviendront comme l’un des clans de Juda, \q et Eqrôn sera comme les Jébusiens.
fr.R: J’ôterai de leur bouche la viande encore pleine de sang, et d’entre leurs dents les aliments impurs. \q Ceux qui resteront appartiendront à notre Dieu. \q Ils seront comme une famille de Juda. \q Eqrôn fera partie du peuple de Dieu, comme les Jébusiens autrefois.

sw.L: Nami nitaiondoa damu yake kinywani mwake, na vitu vyake vya kuchukiza kati ya meno yake; \q naye pia atabaki kwa ajili ya Mungu wetu, \q naye atakuwa kama ukoo katika Yuda, \q na Ekroni kama Myebusi.
sw.B: Nitaiondoa damu vinywani mwao na vyakula vilivyokatazwa kati ya meno yao. \q Watakaobaki watakuwa mali ya Mungu wetu; \q watakuwa kama mmoja wa koo za Yuda, \q na Ekroni itakuwa kama Wayebusi.
sw.R: Nitaondoa vinywani mwao nyama ambayo bado ina damu, na kati ya meno yao vyakula najisi. \q Watakaobaki watakuwa mali ya Mungu wetu. \q Watakuwa kama jamaa moja katika Yuda. \q Ekroni itakuwa sehemu ya watu wa Mungu, kama ilivyokuwa kwa Wayebusi.

vi.L: Ta sẽ cất máu khỏi miệng nó, và các vật đáng ghê tởm khỏi giữa răng nó; \q nó cũng sẽ còn sót lại cho Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta, \q nó sẽ như một thị tộc trong Giu-đa, \q và Éc-rôn như người Giê-bu-sít.
vi.B: Ta sẽ lấy máu ra khỏi miệng chúng và thức ăn bị cấm khỏi giữa răng chúng. \q Những người còn sót lại sẽ thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta; \q họ sẽ trở thành một trong các thị tộc của Giu-đa, \q và Éc-rôn sẽ như người Giê-bu-sít.
vi.R: Ta sẽ lấy khỏi miệng chúng thứ thịt còn máu, và khỏi răng chúng thức ăn ô uế. \q Những người còn sót lại sẽ thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta. \q Họ sẽ như một gia tộc trong Giu-đa. \q Éc-rôn sẽ trở thành một phần của dân Đức Chúa Trời, như người Giê-bu-sít ngày trước.

ko.L: 내가 그의 입에서 피를, 그의 이 사이에서 혐오스러운 것들을 없앨 것이다. \q 그도 남아서 우리 하나님께 속할 것이며, \q 유다의 한 족장같이 될 것이고, \q 에그론은 여부스 사람같이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 그들의 입에서 피를 없애고, 그들의 이 사이에서 금지된 음식을 없앨 것이다. \q 남은 자들은 우리 하나님께 속할 것이다. \q 그들은 유다의 족장들 가운데 하나처럼 되고, \q 에그론은 여부스 사람들처럼 될 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 피가 그대로 있는 고기를 그들의 입에서 빼내고, 부정한 음식을 그들의 이 사이에서 빼낼 것이다. \q 남은 사람들은 우리 하나님께 속할 것이다. \q 그들은 유다의 한 집안처럼 될 것이다. \q 에그론은 여부스 사람들이 그랬던 것처럼 하나님의 백성이 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: the blood and the detestable things: meat eaten with its blood, and unclean food from pagan worship
decisions.reason: The law forbade eating meat with its blood still in it (Leviticus 17:10-14) and named foods that were unclean (Leviticus 11). The "detestable things" are such food, probably eaten in the sacrifices of pagan worship, as in Isaiah 65:4 and 66:17. The LORD will take these from the Philistines' mouths: they will no longer worship as they did. The Hebrew speaks of the Philistines as one person ("his mouth", "his teeth").

decisions.choice: it too will be a remnant for our God: some of the Philistines will be brought into God's people
decisions.reason: The judgment of verses 5-6 is not the end. A remnant will be left, the word used for the survivors of Israel (Isaiah 10:20-22), and it will belong to "our God". Those who were Israel's enemies will be counted with Judah. Isaiah 19:23-25 speaks in the same way of Egypt and Assyria. With "our God" the prophet speaks for a moment in his own voice.

decisions.choice: like a clan in Judah: like one of Judah's own families
decisions.reason: The word can mean a clan or the chief of a clan; Genesis 36:15-43 uses it for the chiefs of Edom. Here it most likely means that the Philistine remnant will have a place among the clans of Judah, as a clan or as its leader.

decisions.choice: like the Jebusite: like the people of Jerusalem before David, who were taken into Israel
decisions.reason: The Jebusites held Jerusalem until David captured it (2 Samuel 5:6-9). They were not wiped out but lived on among Israel (Joshua 15:63); Araunah the Jebusite sold David the threshing floor where the temple was built (2 Samuel 24:18-25). Ekron will be taken in the same way.

decisions.choice: their mouths ... their teeth; those who are left (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the Philistines as one person, which Literal keeps with "its". Balanced and Readable use "their" and "those who are left", so that the reader can follow who is meant.

decisions.choice: meat with blood still in it; unclean food; Ekron will become part of God's people, as the Jebusites did (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the blood and the detestable things (m1) and what it means for Ekron to be like the Jebusites (m4).

decisions.choice: "clan" (L, B); "familia" (R) for 'alluf
decisions.reason: The word used in 12:5-6, so that the passages agree. Literal keeps the Hebrew singular "él" for the Philistines.

decisions.choice: "족장" (L, B); "집안" (R) for 'alluf
decisions.reason: The word used in 12:5-6, as the English "clan" there.

source.text: וְחָנִ֨יתִי לְבֵיתִ֤י מִצָּבָה֙ מֵעֹבֵ֣ר וּמִשָּׁ֔ב וְלֹֽא־יַעֲבֹ֧ר עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם ע֖וֹד נֹגֵ֑שׂ כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְעֵינָֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will encamp at my house [as] a guard, from [one who] passes and from [one who] returns; and will not pass over them again an oppressor, for now I have seen with my eyes.

en.L: And I will encamp at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house [as] a guard against [any] who pass through and return; \q and no oppressor will pass over them again, \q for now I have seen with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes.
en.B: I will camp around {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house to guard it from those who march back and forth. \q No oppressor will overrun them again, \q for now I am watching with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own eyes.
en.R: I will set up camp around {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house to guard it, so that no army can march through it. \q No cruel ruler will ever again overrun {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q because now I am watching over them {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.

es.L: Y acamparé junto a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa [como] guardia contra [los] que pasan y vuelven; \q y no pasará más sobre ellos el opresor, \q porque ahora he visto con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos.
es.B: Acamparé alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa para guardarla de los que marchan de un lado a otro. \q Ningún opresor volverá a invadirlos, \q porque ahora vigilo con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} propios ojos.
es.R: Acamparé alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa para guardarla, para que ningún ejército pueda pasar por ella. \q Ningún gobernante cruel volverá a invadir a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, \q porque ahora los vigilo con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} propios ojos.

fr.L: Et je camperai près de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison [comme] garde contre [ceux] qui passent et qui reviennent ; \q et l’oppresseur ne passera plus sur eux, \q car maintenant j’ai vu de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux.
fr.B: Je camperai autour de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison pour la garder de ceux qui vont et viennent. \q Aucun oppresseur ne les envahira plus, \q car maintenant je veille de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} propres yeux.
fr.R: Je camperai autour de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison pour la garder, et aucune armée ne pourra la traverser. \q Aucun chef cruel n’envahira plus {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, \q car maintenant je veille {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} sur lui.

sw.L: Nami nitapiga kambi kuizunguka nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} [kama] mlinzi dhidi ya wapitao na warudio; \q wala mdhalimu hatapita juu yao tena, \q kwa maana sasa nimeona kwa macho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.B: Nitapiga kambi kuizunguka nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ili kuilinda dhidi ya majeshi yanayopita huku na huko. \q Hakuna mdhalimu atakayewashambulia tena, \q kwa maana sasa ninaangalia kwa macho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mwenyewe.
sw.R: Nitapiga kambi kuizunguka nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ili kuilinda, ili jeshi lolote lisiweze kupita ndani yake. \q Hakuna mtawala katili atakayewashambulia watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} tena, \q kwa sababu sasa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} mwenyewe ninawaangalia.

vi.L: Ta sẽ đóng trại quanh nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [làm] lính canh chống lại kẻ qua người lại; \q kẻ áp bức sẽ không còn đi qua trên họ nữa, \q vì bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy bằng chính mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Ta sẽ đóng trại quanh nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} để canh giữ nó khỏi những kẻ kéo quân qua lại. \q Không kẻ áp bức nào sẽ tràn qua họ nữa, \q vì bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang canh chừng bằng chính mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ta sẽ đóng trại quanh nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} để canh giữ, để không đạo quân nào có thể đi ngang qua. \q Không kẻ cai trị độc ác nào sẽ còn giày xéo dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nữa, \q vì bây giờ chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} canh giữ họ.

ko.L: 내가 내 집을 위하여 진을 쳐서, 지나가고 돌아오는 자들을 막는 파수꾼이 될 것이다. \q 억압하는 자가 다시는 그들 위로 지나가지 못할 것이다. \q 이제 내가 내 눈으로 보았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 내가 내 집 둘레에 진을 치고, 이리저리 행군하는 자들로부터 지킬 것이다. \q 억압하는 자가 다시는 그들을 짓밟지 못할 것이다. \q 이제 내가 내 눈으로 지켜보고 있기 때문이다.
ko.R: 내가 내 집 둘레에 진을 치고 지켜서, 어떤 군대도 지나가지 못하게 하겠다. \q 잔인한 통치자가 다시는 내 백성을 짓밟지 못할 것이다. \q 이제 내가 직접 그들을 지켜보고 있기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: my house: the LORD's temple, and with it his land and people
decisions.reason: "My house" is the temple in Jerusalem, rebuilt in Zechariah's day (1:16; 4:9). Hosea uses "the house of the LORD" for the land and people of Israel as well (Hosea 8:1; 9:15). The next line, "over them", shows that the LORD guards the people, not only the building.

decisions.choice: as a guard, against any who pass through and return: protection from marching armies
alternatives: against an army, against any who pass through and return
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has a word that may be read "against an army" or "as a guard"; the difference is one letter, and the sense is the same. "Those who pass through and return" are armies marching back and forth across the land, as the armies of Egypt and of the northern empires had done for centuries.

decisions.choice: now I have seen with my eyes: the LORD has taken notice and will act
decisions.reason: When the LORD "sees" his people's suffering, he acts to help them, as in Exodus 3:7: "I have surely seen the affliction of my people". The oppression is now in his sight, and he will not let it go on.

decisions.choice: no army can march through it; my people; watching over them myself (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who "they" are and what "seen with my eyes" means (m3). The pronouns for the LORD take the deity_pronoun setting, since the LORD is speaking of himself.

decisions.choice: spans on the free possessives "yangu", "wangu" and on "mimi"
decisions.reason: The LORD's free pronouns take the setting; at the start of a sentence "Nami" is written plainly with its capital.

source.text: גִּילִ֨י מְאֹ֜ד בַּת־צִיּ֗וֹן הָרִ֨יעִי֙ בַּ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הִנֵּ֤ה מַלְכֵּךְ֙ יָ֣בוֹא לָ֔ךְ צַדִּ֥יק וְנוֹשָׁ֖ע ה֑וּא עָנִי֙ וְרֹכֵ֣ב עַל־חֲמ֔וֹר וְעַל־עַ֖יִר בֶּן־אֲתֹנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king comes to you; righteous and saved [is] he, humble and riding on a donkey, and on a colt, [the] son of female donkeys.

en.L: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout aloud, daughter of Jerusalem! \q Look, your king comes to you; \q righteous and victorious [is] he, \q humble and riding on a donkey, \q on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
en.B: Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion! Shout aloud, Daughter Jerusalem! \q Look, your king is coming to you; \q righteous and victorious is he, \q humble and riding on a donkey, \q on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
en.R: Be very glad, people of Zion! Shout for joy, people of Jerusalem! \q Look, your king is coming to you. \q He does what is right, and he has won the victory. \q He comes humble and riding on a donkey, \q on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

es.L: ¡Alégrate mucho, hija de Sion! ¡Grita de júbilo, hija de Jerusalén! \q Mira, tu rey viene a ti; \q justo y victorioso [es] él, \q humilde y montado sobre un asno, \q sobre un pollino, cría de asna.
es.B: ¡Alégrate mucho, hija de Sion! ¡Grita de júbilo, hija de Jerusalén! \q Mira, tu rey está llegando a ti; \q justo y victorioso es él, \q humilde y montado sobre un asno, \q sobre un pollino, cría de asna.
es.R: ¡Alégrate mucho, pueblo de Sion! ¡Grita de alegría, gente de Jerusalén! \q Mira, tu rey viene a ti. \q Él hace lo que es justo, y ha obtenido la victoria. \q Viene humilde y montado sobre un asno, \q sobre un pollino, cría de asna.

fr.L: Réjouis-toi grandement, fille de Sion ! Pousse des cris, fille de Jérusalem ! \q Voici, ton roi vient à toi ; \q juste et victorieux [est]-il, \q humble et monté sur un âne, \q sur un ânon, le petit d’une ânesse.
fr.B: Réjouis-toi grandement, fille de Sion ! Pousse des cris, fille de Jérusalem ! \q Voici, ton roi vient à toi ; \q juste et victorieux, c’est lui, \q humble, monté sur un âne, \q sur un ânon, le petit d’une ânesse.
fr.R: Sois dans la joie, peuple de Sion ! Crie de joie, peuple de Jérusalem ! \q Regarde, ton roi vient à toi. \q Il fait ce qui est juste, et il a remporté la victoire. \q Il vient humble, monté sur un âne, \q sur un ânon, le petit d’une ânesse.

sw.L: Furahi sana, binti Sayuni! Piga kelele kwa shangwe, binti Yerusalemu! \q Tazama, mfalme wako anakujia; \q mwenye haki na mshindi [ni] yeye, \q mnyenyekevu, naye amepanda punda, \q mwana-punda, mtoto wa punda.
sw.B: Furahi sana, Binti Sayuni! Piga kelele kwa shangwe, Binti Yerusalemu! \q Tazama, mfalme wako anakujia; \q yeye ni mwenye haki na mshindi, \q mnyenyekevu, naye amepanda punda, \q mwana-punda, mtoto wa punda.
sw.R: Furahini sana, watu wa Sayuni! Pigeni kelele kwa shangwe, watu wa Yerusalemu! \q Tazameni, mfalme wenu anawajia. \q Yeye hutenda yaliyo haki, naye ameshinda. \q Anakuja akiwa mnyenyekevu, naye amepanda punda, \q mwana-punda, mtoto wa punda.

vi.L: Hỡi con gái Si-ôn, hãy vui mừng lớn tiếng! Hỡi con gái Giê-ru-sa-lem, hãy reo hò! \q Kìa, Vua của ngươi đến với ngươi; \q công chính và đắc thắng [là] người, \q khiêm nhường và cưỡi lừa, \q cưỡi một con lừa con, con của lừa cái.
vi.B: Hỡi con gái Si-ôn, hãy vui mừng lớn tiếng! Hỡi con gái Giê-ru-sa-lem, hãy reo hò! \q Kìa, Vua của ngươi đang đến với ngươi; \q người công chính và đắc thắng, \q khiêm nhường và cưỡi lừa, \q cưỡi một con lừa con, con của lừa cái.
vi.R: Hỡi dân Si-ôn, hãy vui mừng lớn tiếng! Hỡi dân Giê-ru-sa-lem, hãy reo hò! \q Kìa, Vua của các ngươi đang đến với các ngươi. \q Người làm điều ngay thẳng, và người đã chiến thắng. \q Người đến cách khiêm nhường và cưỡi lừa, \q cưỡi một con lừa con, con của lừa cái.

ko.L: 딸 시온아, 크게 기뻐하여라! 딸 예루살렘아, 소리 높여 외쳐라! \q 보라, 네 왕이 네게 온다. \q 그는 의롭고 승리를 얻었으며, \q 겸손하여 나귀를, \q 나귀 새끼인 어린 나귀를 타고 있다.
ko.B: 딸 시온아, 크게 기뻐하여라! 딸 예루살렘아, 소리 높여 외쳐라! \q 보아라, 네 왕이 네게 온다. \q 그는 의롭고 승리를 얻었으며, \q 겸손하여 나귀를, \q 나귀 새끼인 어린 나귀를 타고 있다.
ko.R: 시온 백성아, 크게 기뻐하여라! 예루살렘 백성아, 기뻐 외쳐라! \q 보아라, 너희 왕이 너희에게 온다. \q 그는 옳은 일을 하고, 승리를 얻었다. \q 그는 겸손한 모습으로 나귀를 타고, \q 어미 나귀가 낳은 어린 나귀를 타고 온다.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion, daughter of Jerusalem: the city and its people, pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and stands for the city. The prophets picture the city and its people as a young woman, loved and called to rejoice (Isaiah 62:11; Zephaniah 3:14). The two names say the same thing twice, as Hebrew poetry does.

decisions.choice: righteous and victorious: a just king to whom God has given the victory
alternatives: righteous and bringing salvation (following the Septuagint)
decisions.reason: "Righteous" means that the king rules justly and is in the right before God, as the promised king of David's line will be (Isaiah 9:6; 11:4-5; Jeremiah 23:5). The second word is a passive form of the verb "save": "saved" or "delivered", that is, one whom God has rescued and given victory, as in Psalm 33:16, "a king is not saved by a great army". He does not win by his own strength. The Septuagint reads "saving", a king who saves others.

decisions.choice: humble: lowly, afflicted, not proud
decisions.reason: The word means poor or afflicted, and so humble, the opposite of the proud. It is used of those who suffer and depend on God (Psalm 18:28; Zephaniah 3:12). Matthew 21:5 follows the Greek, which has "gentle".

decisions.choice: riding on a donkey, on a colt: a king who comes in peace, not on a war horse
decisions.reason: Kings rode donkeys and mules in times of peace: David had Solomon ride his own mule to be anointed (1 Kings 1:33), and Genesis 49:11 pictures the ruler from Judah with his donkey's colt. A horse was the animal of war, and verse 10 says that the LORD will take the war horse from Jerusalem. The poem names the animal twice, in parallel, as Hebrew poetry does: "a donkey" and "a colt, the foal of a donkey" are one animal, a young male donkey.

decisions.choice: quoted in Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15 of Jesus' entry into Jerusalem
decisions.reason: When Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey, Matthew and John say that this verse was fulfilled. Matthew 21:5 opens with words from Isaiah 62:11 ("Say to the daughter of Zion") and follows the Greek ("gentle"). Matthew also tells of two animals, a donkey and her colt (Matthew 21:2-7), where the Hebrew names one animal twice; John 12:14-15 speaks of one young donkey. The verse is translated here from the Hebrew as it stands.

decisions.choice: your king: the promised king who comes to Zion
decisions.reason: Zion had no king of its own in Zechariah's day; Judah was a province of Persia. The verse promises that its king will come, as the prophets promised a king of David's line (Jeremiah 23:5; Micah 5:1-3). The verse does not name him. Christians read it of Jesus, as the Gospels do (m5).

decisions.choice: humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey (every level)
decisions.reason: These words are the same at every level, so that the reader can hear them in the Gospels' quotations. Balanced and Readable say "is coming", and Literal and Balanced keep the order of "righteous and victorious is he" as in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: people of Zion, people of Jerusalem; He does what is right, and he has won the victory (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Zion" and "the people of Jerusalem" for "daughter of Zion" and "daughter of Jerusalem", as in Isaiah, and explains "righteous and victorious" (m2).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span for the king
decisions.reason: As with the king of Isaiah 9:6 and 11:1 and the servant of Isaiah 42-53, the pronouns for the king take no deity_pronoun span. The verse speaks of him as a human king, and capital letters would settle a question of interpretation that the text leaves to the reader (m6).

decisions.choice: "hija de Sion", "tu rey viene a ti", "pollino" as Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15; "humilde", not Matthew's "manso"
decisions.reason: The New Testament quotes this verse, so the shared words are worded as the published Spanish Gospels word them. The Hebrew 'ani means humble or lowly (meaning decision m3); Matthew follows the Greek "gentle". Matthew also tells of two animals where the Hebrew names one twice (m5). The king takes no deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "fille de Sion", "ton roi vient à toi", "un ânon" as Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15; "humble", not Matthew's "doux"
decisions.reason: The shared words follow the published French Gospels; 'ani is "humble" (meaning decision m3), where Matthew has "doux" from the Greek, and Matthew's two animals come from his account, not the Hebrew. No deity_pronoun span on the king.

decisions.choice: "binti Sayuni", "mfalme wako anakujia", "mwana-punda" as Matthew 21:5; "mnyenyekevu", not Matthew's "mpole"
decisions.reason: The shared words follow the published Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15; Matthew's "mpole" comes from the Greek. Readable addresses the people in the plural, as Matthew 21:5 R. No deity_pronoun span on the king.

decisions.choice: "Vua của ngươi" (L, B), "Vua của các ngươi" (R) as Matthew 21:5; "khiêm nhường", not Matthew's "hiền lành"
decisions.reason: The quoted words follow the published Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15, "Vua" with a capital as there; the king takes no deity span ("người", lowercase). Matthew's "hiền lành" and his two animals come from the Greek and his account (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: "네 왕이 네게 온다", with no honorific for the king; "겸손하여"
decisions.reason: The king takes no -시-, as the English gives him no deity span (en r-en-3). Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15 say "오신다" of Jesus and Matthew has "온유" from the Greek; this verse is translated from the Hebrew (meaning decisions m3, m5).

source.text: וְהִכְרַתִּי־רֶ֣כֶב מֵאֶפְרַ֗יִם וְסוּס֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְנִכְרְתָה֙ קֶ֣שֶׁת מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְדִבֶּ֥ר שָׁל֖וֹם לַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּמָשְׁלוֹ֙ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־יָ֔ם וּמִנָּהָ֖ר עַד־אַפְסֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will cut off chariot from Ephraim, and horse from Jerusalem, and will be cut off [the] bow of battle; and he will speak peace to the nations, and his rule [will be] from sea to sea, and from [the] River to [the] ends of [the] earth.

en.L: And I will cut off chariotry from Ephraim and horses from Jerusalem, \q and cut off will be the bow of battle; \q and he will speak peace to the nations; \q his rule [will reach] from sea to sea, \q and from the River to [the] ends of [the] earth.
en.B: I will take away the chariots from Ephraim and the war horses from Jerusalem, \q and the battle bow will be broken. \q He will proclaim peace to the nations; \q his rule will stretch from sea to sea, \q from the River to the far ends of the earth.
en.R: I will take away the war chariots from Israel and the war horses from Jerusalem. \q The bows used in battle will be broken. \q Your king will bring peace to the nations. \q He will rule over all the land between the seas, \q from the Euphrates River to the farthest places on earth.

es.L: Y cortaré los carros de Efraín y los caballos de Jerusalén, \q y será cortado el arco de guerra; \q y él hablará paz a las naciones; \q su dominio [será] de mar a mar, \q y desde el Río hasta [los] confines de [la] tierra.
es.B: Quitaré los carros de Efraín y los caballos de guerra de Jerusalén, \q y el arco de guerra será quebrado. \q Él proclamará paz a las naciones; \q su reino se extenderá de mar a mar, \q desde el Río hasta los extremos de la tierra.
es.R: Quitaré los carros de guerra de Israel y los caballos de guerra de Jerusalén. \q Los arcos que se usan en la batalla serán quebrados. \q Tu rey traerá paz a las naciones. \q Reinará sobre toda la tierra que hay entre los mares, \q desde el río Éufrates hasta los lugares más lejanos de la tierra.

fr.L: Et je retrancherai les chars d’Éphraïm et les chevaux de Jérusalem, \q et l’arc de guerre sera retranché ; \q et il parlera de paix aux nations ; \q sa domination [ira] d’une mer à l’autre mer, \q et depuis le Fleuve jusqu’aux extrémités de [la] terre.
fr.B: J’ôterai les chars d’Éphraïm et les chevaux de guerre de Jérusalem, \q et l’arc de guerre sera brisé. \q Il proclamera la paix aux nations ; \q son pouvoir s’étendra d’une mer à l’autre, \q depuis le Fleuve jusqu’au bout de la terre.
fr.R: J’ôterai les chars de guerre d’Israël et les chevaux de guerre de Jérusalem. \q Les arcs de guerre seront brisés. \q Ton roi apportera la paix aux nations. \q Il régnera sur tout le pays entre les mers, \q depuis le fleuve Euphrate jusqu’aux endroits les plus lointains de la terre.

sw.L: Nami nitakatilia mbali magari ya vita kutoka Efraimu, na farasi kutoka Yerusalemu, \q na upinde wa vita utakatiliwa mbali; \q naye atanena amani kwa mataifa; \q utawala wake [utakuwa] kutoka bahari hata bahari, \q na kutoka Mto hata miisho ya dunia.
sw.B: Nitaondoa magari ya vita kutoka Efraimu na farasi wa vita kutoka Yerusalemu, \q na upinde wa vita utavunjwa. \q Atatangaza amani kwa mataifa; \q utawala wake utaenea kutoka bahari hata bahari, \q kutoka Mto hata miisho ya mbali ya dunia.
sw.R: Nitaondoa magari ya vita kutoka Israeli na farasi wa vita kutoka Yerusalemu. \q Pinde zinazotumika vitani zitavunjwa. \q Mfalme wenu ataleta amani kwa mataifa. \q Atatawala nchi yote kati ya bahari, \q kutoka Mto Frati mpaka mahali pa mbali kabisa duniani.

vi.L: Ta sẽ diệt trừ xe chiến mã khỏi Ép-ra-im, và ngựa khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q cung chiến trận sẽ bị diệt trừ; \q người sẽ rao bình an cho các nước; \q quyền cai trị của người [sẽ] từ biển này đến biển kia, \q và từ Sông Cái đến [tận] cùng trái đất.
vi.B: Ta sẽ cất bỏ xe chiến mã khỏi Ép-ra-im và ngựa chiến khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q và cung chiến trận sẽ bị bẻ gãy. \q Người sẽ công bố bình an cho các nước; \q quyền cai trị của người sẽ trải từ biển này đến biển kia, \q từ Sông Cái đến tận cùng trái đất.
vi.R: Ta sẽ cất bỏ xe chiến mã khỏi Y-sơ-ra-ên và ngựa chiến khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem. \q Cung tên dùng trong chiến trận sẽ bị bẻ gãy. \q Vua của các ngươi sẽ đem bình an đến cho các nước. \q Người sẽ cai trị cả vùng đất giữa các biển, \q từ sông Ơ-phơ-rát đến những nơi xa nhất trên mặt đất.

ko.L: 내가 에브라임에서 병거를, 예루살렘에서 말을 끊을 것이며, \q 전쟁의 활도 끊어질 것이다. \q 그가 민족들에게 평화를 말할 것이며, \q 그의 다스림이 바다에서 바다까지, \q 강에서 땅끝까지 [이를 것이다].
ko.B: 내가 에브라임에서 병거를 없애고 예루살렘에서 군마를 없앨 것이며, \q 전쟁에 쓰는 활도 꺾일 것이다. \q 그는 민족들에게 평화를 선포할 것이며, \q 그의 다스림이 바다에서 바다까지, \q 그 강에서 땅 끝까지 미칠 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 이스라엘에서 전차를 없애고 예루살렘에서 군마를 없앨 것이다. \q 전쟁에 쓰는 활은 꺾일 것이다. \q 너희 왕이 민족들에게 평화를 가져다줄 것이다. \q 그는 바다와 바다 사이의 온 땅을 다스릴 것이다. \q 유프라테스 강에서 땅의 가장 먼 곳까지 다스릴 것이다.

decisions.choice: I will cut off the chariot, the horse and the bow: the LORD himself ends war
decisions.reason: Chariots, horses and bows were the weapons of war. The LORD takes them away from his own people, from Ephraim (the northern tribes) and Jerusalem alike, so that the king of verse 9 rules without them. Peace comes as the LORD's gift, not by force of arms (Hosea 2:20; Micah 5:9-10; Psalm 46:10). The Septuagint reads "he will cut off", making the king the one who acts.

decisions.choice: Ephraim and Jerusalem: the northern and southern kingdoms, one people again
decisions.reason: Ephraim stands for the northern tribes of Israel, which had been taken into exile by Assyria two centuries before; Jerusalem for Judah. The promise is for all Israel, reunited under one king (10:6; Ezekiel 37:15-22).

decisions.choice: speak peace to the nations: announce peace, and bring it about
decisions.reason: To "speak peace" is to declare an end of hostility and to offer friendship (Esther 9:30; Psalm 85:9). The king's word to the nations is peace, where kings usually spoke war.

decisions.choice: his rule from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth: the words of Psalm 72:8
decisions.reason: The line repeats Psalm 72:8, a prayer for the king of David's line, and is translated with the same words. "The River" is the Euphrates; "from sea to sea" may mean from the Dead Sea to the Mediterranean, or simply the whole earth. The king's rule has no limit.

decisions.choice: the wording of Psalm 72:8 at each level
decisions.reason: The last two lines reuse the published wording of Psalm 72:8 at each level (m4). Readable says "Israel" for Ephraim and "your king" for "he", so that the reader can tell who is meant (m2), and Balanced and Readable say "war horses" and "broken" for the bow.

decisions.choice: the last two lines reuse Spanish Psalm 72:8 at each level, with the wish turned into a promise
decisions.reason: As the English (m4), the words of Psalm 72:8 are kept ("de mar a mar", "desde el Río hasta [los] confines de [la] tierra"; "los extremos de la tierra"; "el río Éufrates ... los lugares más lejanos"), with future verbs in place of the psalm's "may".

decisions.choice: the last two lines reuse French Psalm 72:8 at each level
decisions.reason: "d'une mer à l'autre", "depuis le Fleuve jusqu'aux extrémités de [la] terre" (L), "jusqu'au bout de la terre" (B), "le fleuve Euphrate ... les plus lointains" (R), with the future for the psalm's wish.

decisions.choice: the last two lines reuse Swahili Psalm 72:8 at each level
decisions.reason: "kutoka bahari hata bahari, na kutoka Mto hata miisho ya dunia" and its B and R forms, with the future for the psalm's wish.

decisions.choice: the last two lines reuse Vietnamese Psalm 72:8 ("từ biển này đến biển kia", "từ Sông Cái đến [tận] cùng trái đất"); "rao", not "phán", for the king
decisions.reason: The psalm's words are kept at each level. "phán" is kept for God, so the king "rao" or "công bố" peace.

decisions.choice: the last two lines reuse Korean Psalm 72:8 ("바다에서 바다까지, 강에서 땅끝까지")
decisions.reason: The psalm's words are kept at each level, with the future in place of its prayer; the king takes no -시-.

source.text: גַּם־אַ֣תְּ בְּדַם־בְּרִיתֵ֗ךְ שִׁלַּ֤חְתִּי אֲסִירַ֨יִךְ֙מִבּ֔וֹר אֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Also you, by [the] blood of your covenant, I will send out your prisoners from a pit [in which there is] no water in it.

en.L: You also, because of the blood of your covenant, \q I will set your prisoners free from the pit [that has] no water in it.
en.B: As for you, because of the blood of your covenant, \q I will set your prisoners free from the waterless pit.
en.R: As for you, people of Zion, I made a covenant with you and sealed it with blood. \q Because of that, I will set your prisoners free from the dry pit.

es.L: Y tú también, por la sangre de tu pacto, \q soltaré a tus prisioneros del pozo [en que] no hay agua.
es.B: En cuanto a ti, por la sangre de tu pacto, \q soltaré a tus prisioneros del pozo sin agua.
es.R: En cuanto a ti, pueblo de Sion, hice un pacto contigo y lo sellé con sangre. \q Por eso libertaré a tus prisioneros del pozo seco.

fr.L: Toi aussi, à cause du sang de ton alliance, \q je libérerai tes captifs de la fosse [où il n’y a] pas d’eau.
fr.B: Quant à toi, à cause du sang de ton alliance, \q je libérerai tes captifs de la fosse sans eau.
fr.R: Quant à toi, peuple de Sion, j’ai fait alliance avec toi et je l’ai scellée par le sang. \q C’est pourquoi je libérerai tes captifs de la fosse sèche.

sw.L: Nawe pia, kwa sababu ya damu ya agano lako, \q nitawaachilia wafungwa wako kutoka shimo lisilo na maji ndani yake.
sw.B: Na kwa habari yako, kwa sababu ya damu ya agano lako, \q nitawaachilia wafungwa wako kutoka shimo lisilo na maji.
sw.R: Na ninyi, watu wa Sayuni, nilifanya agano nanyi na kulithibitisha kwa damu. \q Kwa sababu hiyo nitawaachilia wafungwa wenu kutoka shimo kavu.

vi.L: Còn ngươi nữa, vì huyết của giao ước ngươi, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ thả những tù nhân của ngươi ra khỏi hố không có nước.
vi.B: Còn về phần con, vì huyết của giao ước với con, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giải thoát những tù nhân của con khỏi hố khô.
vi.R: Còn các con, hỡi dân Si-ôn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã lập giao ước với các con và đóng ấn bằng huyết. \q Vì vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giải thoát những tù nhân của các con khỏi hố khô.

ko.L: 또 너는, 네 언약의 피 때문에, \q 내가 네 갇힌 자들을 물 없는 구덩이에서 놓아 보낼 것이다.
ko.B: 너에게는, 너와 맺은 언약의 피 때문에, \q 내가 네 갇힌 자들을 물 없는 구덩이에서 풀어 줄 것이다.
ko.R: 시온 백성아, 내가 너희와 언약을 맺고 피로 그것을 확증했다. \q 그러므로 내가 너희 가운데 갇힌 사람들을 마른 구덩이에서 풀어 주겠다.

decisions.choice: you: Zion, addressed again
decisions.reason: The "you" is feminine singular, so the LORD now speaks to Daughter Zion of verse 9. The prisoners are her own people, still scattered among the nations.

decisions.choice: the blood of your covenant: the covenant made at Sinai and sealed with blood
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses threw the blood of the sacrifices on the people and said, "Look, the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you" (Exodus 24:8). Because of that covenant, the LORD will not leave his people in captivity. At the Last Supper Jesus speaks of the cup as "my blood of the covenant" (Matthew 26:28; Mark 14:24).

decisions.choice: the pit with no water in it: a dry cistern used as a prison
decisions.reason: Cisterns cut into the rock held rainwater; an empty one made a prison from which no one could climb out. Joseph's brothers threw him into such a pit (Genesis 37:24), and Jeremiah was let down into one (Jeremiah 38:6). Exile is pictured as such a pit.

decisions.choice: people of Zion; I made a covenant with you and sealed it with blood (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names who is spoken to (m1) and explains "the blood of your covenant" (m2) in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: "tú", Zion addressed in the singular
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is feminine singular, Daughter Zion (meaning decision m1), so Spanish says "tú" with no plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Zion with "con" (B) / "các con" (R) in 9:11-13; "ngươi" (L)
decisions.reason: The promise to Zion takes the tender address set at 2:14-15 for God speaking to his city; 9:9-10 keep "Vua của ngươi" / "Vua của các ngươi" because they are the words Matthew 21:5 quotes. Greece, addressed in 9:13, stays "ngươi".

source.text: שׁ֚וּבוּ לְבִצָּר֔וֹן אֲסִירֵ֖י הַתִּקְוָ֑ה גַּם־הַיּ֕וֹם מַגִּ֥יד מִשְׁנֶ֖ה אָשִׁ֥יב לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Return to [the] stronghold, prisoners of the hope; also today [I am] declaring [that] double I will restore to you.

en.L: Return to [the] stronghold, \q prisoners of hope; \q even today I am declaring: \q double I will restore to you.
en.B: Come back to the stronghold, \q you prisoners who have hope! \q Even today I announce \q that I will give back to you double.
en.R: You prisoners who still have hope, \q come back to the place where you will be safe! \q Today I promise you \q that I will give you back twice as much as you lost.

es.L: {{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} a [la] fortaleza, \q prisioneros de la esperanza; \q aun hoy declaro: \q el doble te devolveré.
es.B: {{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} a la fortaleza, \q ¡prisioneros que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} esperanza! \q Hoy mismo anuncio \q que te devolveré el doble.
es.R: Prisioneros que todavía {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} esperanza, \q ¡{{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} al lugar donde {{plural_you:estarán|estaréis}} seguros! \q Hoy te prometo \q que te devolveré el doble de lo que perdiste.

fr.L: Revenez à [la] forteresse, \q captifs de l’espérance ; \q aujourd’hui même je le déclare : \q je te rendrai le double.
fr.B: Revenez à la forteresse, \q captifs pleins d’espérance ! \q Aujourd’hui même, je l’annonce : \q je te rendrai le double.
fr.R: Captifs qui avez encore de l’espoir, \q revenez là où vous serez en sécurité ! \q Aujourd’hui, je te le promets : \q je te rendrai deux fois plus que ce que tu as perdu.

sw.L: Rudini kwenye ngome, \q enyi wafungwa wa tumaini; \q hata leo ninatangaza: \q nitakurudishia maradufu.
sw.B: Rudini kwenye ngome, \q enyi wafungwa wenye tumaini! \q Hata leo ninatangaza \q kwamba nitakurudishia maradufu.
sw.R: Enyi wafungwa ambao bado mna tumaini, \q rudini mahali mtakapokuwa salama! \q Leo ninawaahidi \q kwamba nitawarudishia mara mbili ya kile mlichopoteza.

vi.L: Hãy trở về đồn lũy, \q hỡi những tù nhân của hy vọng; \q ngay hôm nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tuyên bố: \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ hoàn lại cho ngươi gấp đôi.
vi.B: Hãy trở về đồn lũy, \q hỡi những tù nhân đầy hy vọng! \q Ngay hôm nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} công bố \q rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ hoàn lại cho con gấp đôi.
vi.R: Hỡi những tù nhân vẫn còn hy vọng, \q hãy trở về nơi các con sẽ được an toàn! \q Hôm nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hứa với các con \q rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đền lại gấp đôi những gì các con đã mất.

ko.L: 요새로 돌아오너라, \q 소망의 갇힌 자들아. \q 오늘도 내가 선언한다. \q 내가 네게 갑절로 갚아 주겠다.
ko.B: 요새로 돌아오너라, \q 소망을 품은 갇힌 자들아! \q 오늘 내가 선언한다. \q 내가 네게 갑절로 돌려주겠다.
ko.R: 아직 소망을 품은 갇힌 사람들아, \q 안전한 곳으로 돌아오너라! \q 오늘 내가 너희에게 약속한다. \q 너희가 잃은 것의 두 배를 돌려주겠다.

decisions.choice: return to the stronghold: come home to the place of safety
decisions.reason: The stronghold is a fortified place where people are safe. Here it is Zion, or the LORD himself, who is called his people's stronghold in Joel 4:16 and Nahum 1:7. The prisoners in the pit of verse 11 are called to come home.

decisions.choice: prisoners of hope: captives who have reason to hope
decisions.reason: The captives are not without hope, because the LORD has promised to free them. Hope here is the confident waiting for what God will do (Jeremiah 29:11; 31:17).

decisions.choice: I will restore to you double: twice as much as was lost
decisions.reason: A double share was the portion of the firstborn (Deuteronomy 21:17). Isaiah 61:7 promises a double share in place of shame, and Isaiah 40:2 says that Jerusalem has received double for her sins; Job received back twice what he had lost (Job 42:10). The LORD's restoring will be more than full.

decisions.choice: the place where you will be safe; twice as much as you lost (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "stronghold" (m1) and "double" (m3), and puts the address to the prisoners first.

decisions.choice: "revenez" to the captives, "te" to Zion
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls the prisoners in the plural and then promises Zion in the singular; French keeps the change of number, as the Hebrew does.

source.text: כִּֽי־דָרַ֨כְתִּי לִ֜י יְהוּדָ֗ה קֶ֚שֶׁת מִלֵּ֣אתִי אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְעוֹרַרְתִּ֤י בָנַ֨יִךְ֙ צִיּ֔וֹן עַל־בָּנַ֖יִךְ יָוָ֑ן וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךְ כְּחֶ֥רֶב גִּבּֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: For I will bend for myself Judah [as] a bow; I will fill [it with] Ephraim, and I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece; and I will make you like [the] sword of a warrior.

en.L: For I will bend Judah for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} [as a bow]; I will fill the bow [with] Ephraim; \q and I will rouse your sons, Zion, \q against your sons, Greece, \q and I will make you like a warrior's sword.
en.B: For I will bend Judah as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bow and set Ephraim on it as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arrow. \q I will rouse your sons, Zion, \q against your sons, Greece, \q and make you like a warrior's sword.
en.R: I will use Judah as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bow and Ephraim as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arrow. \q People of Zion, I will send your sons into battle \q against the sons of Greece. \q I will make you like a soldier's sword.

es.L: Porque tensaré a Judá para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} [como un arco]; llenaré el arco [con] Efraín; \q y despertaré a tus hijos, Sion, \q contra tus hijos, Grecia, \q y te haré como espada de guerrero.
es.B: Porque tensaré a Judá como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} arco y pondré a Efraín en él como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} flecha. \q Despertaré a tus hijos, Sion, \q contra tus hijos, Grecia, \q y te haré como espada de guerrero.
es.R: Usaré a Judá como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} arco y a Efraín como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} flecha. \q Pueblo de Sion, enviaré a tus hijos a la batalla \q contra los hijos de Grecia. \q Te haré como la espada de un soldado.

fr.L: Car je tendrai Juda pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} [comme un arc] ; je remplirai l’arc [d’]Éphraïm ; \q et je réveillerai tes fils, Sion, \q contre tes fils, Grèce, \q et je ferai de toi comme l’épée d’un guerrier.
fr.B: Car je tendrai Juda comme {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} arc, et j’y placerai Éphraïm comme {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} flèche. \q Je réveillerai tes fils, Sion, \q contre tes fils, Grèce, \q et je ferai de toi comme l’épée d’un guerrier.
fr.R: Je me servirai de Juda comme de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} arc et d’Éphraïm comme de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} flèche. \q Peuple de Sion, j’enverrai tes fils au combat \q contre les fils de la Grèce. \q Je ferai de toi comme l’épée d’un soldat.

sw.L: Kwa maana nitampinda Yuda kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} [kama upinde]; nitaujaza upinde [kwa] Efraimu; \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawaamsha wana wako, ee Sayuni, \q dhidi ya wana wako, ee Ugiriki, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakufanya kama upanga wa shujaa.
sw.B: Kwa maana nitampinda Yuda kama upinde {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, na kumweka Efraimu juu yake kama mshale {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Nitawaamsha wana wako, ee Sayuni, \q dhidi ya wana wako, ee Ugiriki, \q na kukufanya kama upanga wa shujaa.
sw.R: Nitamtumia Yuda kama upinde {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} na Efraimu kama mshale {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Enyi watu wa Sayuni, nitawapeleka wana wenu vitani \q dhidi ya wana wa Ugiriki. \q Nitawafanya kama upanga wa askari.

vi.L: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giương Giu-đa cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [như cây cung]; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ lắp Ép-ra-im [vào] cung; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ khơi dậy con cái ngươi, hỡi Si-ôn, \q chống lại con cái ngươi, hỡi Hy Lạp, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho ngươi như gươm của dũng sĩ.
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giương Giu-đa làm cung của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và lắp Ép-ra-im làm mũi tên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Hỡi Si-ôn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ khơi dậy con cái của con \q chống lại con cái ngươi, hỡi Hy Lạp, \q và làm cho con như gươm của dũng sĩ.
vi.R: Ta sẽ dùng Giu-đa làm cây cung của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và Ép-ra-im làm mũi tên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Hỡi dân Si-ôn, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai con cái các con ra trận \q chống lại con cái Hy Lạp. \q Ta sẽ làm cho các con như thanh gươm của người lính.

ko.L: 내가 나를 위하여 유다를 [활처럼] 당기고, 에브라임으로 [그 활을] 채울 것이다. \q 시온아, 내가 네 아들들을 일으켜 \q 그리스야, 네 아들들을 치게 하고, \q 너를 용사의 칼같이 만들 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 유다를 내 활로 당기고, 에브라임을 내 화살로 메길 것이다. \q 시온아, 내가 네 아들들을 일으켜 \q 그리스야, 네 아들들과 맞서게 하고, \q 너를 용사의 칼처럼 만들 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 유다를 내 활로 쓰고 에브라임을 내 화살로 쓰겠다. \q 시온 백성아, 내가 너희 아들들을 전쟁에 내보내어 \q 그리스의 아들들과 싸우게 하겠다. \q 내가 너희를 군인의 칼처럼 만들겠다.

decisions.choice: bend Judah as a bow, fill it with Ephraim: Judah and Ephraim are the LORD's weapons
decisions.reason: A bow was "bent" (strung and drawn) to shoot, and "filled" when the arrow was set on it. The LORD himself is the warrior; Judah is his bow and Ephraim his arrow. The two kingdoms fight together again as one people, under the LORD's hand.

decisions.choice: Greece: the Greeks (Javan), the peoples of the far west
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name is Javan, the Ionians, used for the Greeks (Genesis 10:2-5; Isaiah 66:19; Joel 4:6; Daniel 8:21). In Zechariah's day Greek cities were at war with Persia; later, Alexander the Great and the kingdoms that followed him ruled the land of Israel. Readers who date these chapters later see the Greek kingdoms here; others take Greece as the distant enemy of the day. The oracle does not say.

decisions.choice: your sons, Zion ... your sons, Greece: two cities addressed in turn
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks first to Zion and then to Greece, setting the people of each against the other. The last line returns to Zion: "I will make you like a warrior's sword".

decisions.choice: as my bow ... as my arrow (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the bow and the arrow, which Literal brackets, so that the picture of the bow being drawn (m1) is clear. The LORD speaks of himself, so "my" takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: I will send your sons into battle against the sons of Greece; a soldier's sword (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "rouse your sons against your sons" means, and puts the address to Zion first.

decisions.choice: "Grecia" for Javan
decisions.reason: The English says "Greece" at every level, so Spanish does too (Javán is kept where the English keeps Javan).

decisions.choice: "Ugiriki" for Javan
decisions.reason: The English says "Greece", so Swahili uses Ugiriki, as Acts 20:2.

decisions.choice: "Hy Lạp" for Javan
decisions.reason: The English says "Greece"; "Gia-van" is kept where the English keeps Javan.

decisions.choice: "그리스" for Javan
decisions.reason: The English says "Greece", so Korean uses 그리스, as Acts and Daniel.

source.text: וַֽיהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יֵֽרָאֶ֔ה וְיָצָ֥א כַבָּרָ֖ק חִצּ֑וֹ וַֽאדֹנָ֤י יְהֹוִה֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֣ר יִתְקָ֔ע וְהָלַ֖ךְ בְּסַעֲר֥וֹת תֵּימָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh over them will appear, and will go out like lightning his arrow; and [the] Lord Yahweh on the horn will blow, and he will go in [the] storms of [the] south.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will appear over them, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arrow will go out like lightning; \q and the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will blow on the trumpet \q and march in the storms of the south.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will appear above them, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arrow will flash out like lightning. \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will sound the ram's horn \q and march out in the storm winds from the south.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will appear above {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. \q His arrows will flash like lightning. \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will blow the trumpet. \q He will march out in the storms from the south.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} aparecerá sobre ellos, \q y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} flecha saldrá como relámpago; \q y el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} tocará la trompeta \q y marchará en las tempestades del sur.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} aparecerá sobre ellos, \q y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} flecha brillará como el relámpago. \q El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} tocará el cuerno de carnero \q y avanzará en los vientos tempestuosos del sur.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} aparecerá sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo. \q Sus flechas brillarán como relámpagos. \q El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} tocará la trompeta. \q Avanzará en las tormentas del sur.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} apparaîtra au-dessus d’eux, \q et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} flèche partira comme l’éclair ; \q et le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} sonnera du cor \q et marchera dans les tempêtes du sud.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} apparaîtra au-dessus d’eux, \q et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} flèche jaillira comme l’éclair. \q Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} sonnera du cor \q et s’avancera dans les vents de tempête du sud.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} apparaîtra au-dessus de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple. \q Ses flèches brilleront comme des éclairs. \q Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} sonnera de la trompette. \q Il s’avancera dans les tempêtes du sud.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataonekana juu yao, \q na mshale {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} utatoka kama umeme; \q na Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} atapiga baragumu \q na kwenda katika dhoruba za kusini.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataonekana juu yao, \q na mshale {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} utamulika kama umeme. \q Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} atapiga baragumu \q na kusonga mbele katika pepo za dhoruba za kusini.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataonekana juu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. \q Mishale {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} itamulika kama umeme. \q Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} atapiga baragumu. \q Atasonga mbele katika dhoruba za kusini.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ hiện ra trên họ, \q và mũi tên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ bay ra như chớp; \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ thổi kèn \q và tiến bước trong các cơn bão phương nam.
vi.B: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ hiện ra trên họ, \q và mũi tên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ lóe ra như chớp. \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ thổi tù và \q và tiến ra trong những cơn gió bão từ phương nam.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ hiện ra trên dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Những mũi tên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ lóe sáng như chớp. \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ thổi kèn. \q Ngài sẽ tiến ra trong những cơn bão từ phương nam.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들 위에 나타나시고, \q 그분의 화살이 번개같이 나갈 것이다. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나팔을 부시고 \q 남쪽의 폭풍 속에서 행진하실 것이다.
ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들 위에 나타나시고, \q 그분의 화살이 번개처럼 번쩍일 것이다. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 숫양 뿔 나팔을 부시고 \q 남쪽에서 불어오는 폭풍을 타고 나아가실 것이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 백성 위에 나타나실 것이다. \q 그분의 화살들이 번개처럼 번쩍일 것이다. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 나팔을 부실 것이다. \q 그분께서 남쪽에서 오는 폭풍 속에서 나아가실 것이다.

decisions.choice: the LORD will appear: he comes as a warrior, in the storm
decisions.reason: The prophets and psalms picture the LORD coming to fight for his people in a storm: his arrows are lightning and his voice is thunder (Psalm 18:8-16; 77:18-19; Habakkuk 3:3-11). Here he appears above his people as they fight (verse 13), and the battle is his.

decisions.choice: blow on the trumpet: the signal for battle
decisions.reason: The ram's horn was blown to call to battle and to sound the attack (Judges 3:27; Joshua 6:5). Here it is the Lord GOD himself who sounds it.

decisions.choice: the storms of the south: the LORD comes from the southern desert, from Sinai
decisions.reason: The south (Teman) is the land toward Edom and Sinai. The old poems tell of the LORD marching from there to help his people (Deuteronomy 33:2; Judges 5:4; Habakkuk 3:3). Storms from the southern desert were fierce (Isaiah 21:1).

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R); ram's horn (B)
decisions.reason: The shofar is a "trumpet" at Literal and Readable and a "ram's horn" at Balanced, as in Isaiah. Readable says "his people" for "them" and "arrows" for the single arrow, since lightning flashes again and again.

decisions.choice: "trompeta" (L, R); "cuerno de carnero" (B); "el Señor DIOS"
decisions.reason: The shofar follows the wording set in Isaiah at each level; Adonai YHWH is "el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}", with the article outside the span.

decisions.choice: "Mishale yake" takes a span
decisions.reason: The English Readable starts the sentence with "His", which needs no span; in Swahili the possessive stands after the noun, in mid-sentence, so it takes the setting.

decisions.choice: "kèn" (L, R); "tù và" (B); "Chúa là CHÚA" for the Lord GOD
decisions.reason: The shofar follows the Isaiah wording at each level.

decisions.choice: "나팔" (L, R); "숫양 뿔 나팔" (B); "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서"
decisions.reason: The shofar as Jeremiah and Isaiah; after the Lord GOD span only 께서 is used, so that both readings of the span take the same particle. The prophet speaks about God, so the honorific is used.

source.text: יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֮ יָגֵ֣ן עֲלֵיהֶם֒ וְאָכְל֗וּ וְכָֽבְשׁוּ֙ אַבְנֵי־קֶ֔לַע וְשָׁת֥וּ הָמ֖וּ כְּמוֹ־יָ֑יִן וּמָֽלְאוּ֙ כַּמִּזְרָ֔ק כְּזָוִיּ֖וֹת מִזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh of hosts will defend them, and they will devour and tread down [the] stones of [the] sling, and they will drink [and] roar like wine, and they will be full like the bowl, like [the] corners of [the] altar.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will defend them, \q and they will devour and tread down the sling stones; \q and they will drink, they will be loud as [with] wine, \q and they will be full like the bowl, \q like the corners of [the] altar.
